Hidden cost for the performance lens: every vendor send() now goes through session.bytes(for:) and iterates AsyncBytes one byte at a time, calling Task.checkCancellation() per byte (HTTPClient.swift:176-183). Before, it was a single data(for:) call. This is negligible at ~4 KB payloads every 300 s, but a chunked read, or checking cancellation every N bytes, would avoid per-byte overhead near the 8 MiB cap.

PERF (low): HTTPClient.readBounded (Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Networking/HTTPClient.swift:177) reads one byte per iteration and calls Task.checkCancellation() per byte. Measured with -O: 4 KB goes from 0.105 to 0.187 ms, 1 MiB goes from 0.18 to 21.4 ms (about 115x). This now applies to every vendor fetch, not just status sources. Reading bytes in chunks, or using a URLSessionDataDelegate that counts didReceive data, would remove the cost.
CORRECTNESS

LEAK (residual, low): BoundedProcess drain threads (Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Util/BoundedProcess.swift `drain`) block in availableData or readDataToEndOfFile until every holder of the pipe's write end closes it. A grandchild that inherits the pipe (for example an agy daemon, which was not confirmed) keeps one GCD thread and one fd pinned after run() returns. Only the direct child is ever killed; there is no process-group kill.
